shots.storyline: Indoor badminton hall with a blue court, green run-off areas, a taut net on yellow posts, overhead sponsor banners (YONEX / 旭日星空 / XURI STAR) and a top-right channel watermark. The supplied segment contains two internal camera cuts (≈3.9 s and ≈7.6 s), so three distinct views are present and person identity is not carried across them. In the first view (0.0-3.8 s) the near-side player P01 (black tee, grey shorts, back to camera) faces the far-side player P02 (pink shirt). P02 twice raises his racket overhead and delivers shuttles across the net; P01 steps out to his own right (screen-right) into a loaded sideways reach for each delivery and answers with a rising return back over the net (the second return is tracked arcing over the net and descending into the far right court at 3.2-3.8 s), then re-spreads into a wide ready stance between deliveries. At the first cut the pairing and roles change: in the second view (3.9-7.6 s) the near-side player P03 (black sleeveless top, back to camera) keeps a racket low in his left hand and tosses shuttles from his raised bare right hand, while the far-side player P04 (maroon shirt, light shorts) lunges forward or sideways to play each tossed shuttle with a rising return and then resets upright; P03 stays largely stationary between tosses, consistent with a feeder role. At the second cut (≈7.6 s) the camera shows a single presenter P05 facing the lens in a black ACTIVE T-shirt and pink shorts, smiling and waving the raised racket in a conversational manner (no stroke is performed); in the final frame a Chinese subtitle appears at the bottom of the screen. Action preparations at 0.0 s and at the 3.9 s view start are cropped because the racket/hand is already raised in the first observed frame of each view.

uncertainties: The segment contains two internal camera cuts (≈3.9 s and ≈7.6 s); clothing and pairings differ between views, so identity continuity of P01/P03/P05 (and P02/P04) is not established and is not assumed.

P03's deliveries are labelled hand feed because the shuttle is visibly released from his raised bare hand while the racket is held low in the other hand; whether any frame of a racket strike was missed between samples cannot be excluded, but no racket-shuttle contact is visible for these deliveries.

P02's deliveries are labelled racket feed based on the visible overhead swing correlated with the shuttle departing toward P01; no underarm serving mechanics or explicit start-of-play context is shown, so they are not serves.
Exact racket-shuttle contact instants for P01's and P04's returns fall between sampled frames and are estimated; outgoing shuttle landings are not observed for the first returns of each view.

P01's and P04's stroke subtypes are recorded as upward return: the rising outgoing paths are observed (and for P01's second return the shuttle is tracked descending into the far right court), but the contact origins are not firmly resolved as forecourt, so lift/clear subtypes are not claimed.
P03's dominant striking hand and P05's handedness are not clearly determinable from the back-facing / gesturing views.

The final-frame Chinese subtitle indicates on-screen text only; no audio was supplied to this visual stage, so no speech is asserted for P05 despite his mouth movement and racket gestures (treated as conversational, not a stroke).
